question: What will the United States national average gas price be on November 3, 2026?

calls.reasoning: AAA national average is $4.356 on Oct 12 (month ago $4.31, Oct 1 $4.41), flat to slightly down. Nov RBOB futures of about $3.31 plus roughly $1.05 for taxes and margin give about $4.36, so retail is near equilibrium. Seasonal drift from mid-Oct to early Nov (winter blend) is a few cents lower, so the median is about $4.31. Crude is high and volatile (WTI ~$90, Brent ~$103, Gulf conflict), so the tails are widened. Manifold's related market 'What will the US average gas price hit in October 2026?' (448 trades, 13 holders, closes Oct 31) gives 73% that the average touches <=$4.30 at some point in October and ~13% that it touches >=$4.55; it measures a touch at any time in October, not the Nov 3 value, so it is used only as supporting evidence of a mild downward drift. Harness found no market on Polymarket or Manifold for this exact question; Kalshi and bookmakers were not checked.

calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on the AAA level ($4.356), the trend and the seasonality. Factual disputes: (1) RBOB at $3.31-3.32 (Oct 2-10, Runs 1 and 2) vs $3.15 on Oct 12 (Run 3, fueldataportal). These may be different contracts or sources, and it can't be settled without web access, so wholesale-implied fair value is carried as $4.15-4.42. (2) Brent on Oct 12 at $103-104 vs $106-108; Run 3 cites a specific same-day escalation, so I leave some extra upside. (3) Kalshi: Runs 2 and 3 independently report the same Oct 8 prices on the same AAA Nov 3 contract, which I treat as credible (Run 1 didn't check Kalshi); liquidity is unverified. Judgment: weigh trend extrapolation ($4.29), the Kalshi median (~$4.22) and seasonality, giving a median of $4.26. Width sits between the runs' widths on the regime evidence, not by averaging. No escape mass: there is no plausible mechanism to move below $3.50 or above $6 in 22 days.
